problem: Existing social navigation simulation and benchmarking platforms are fragmented, tied to specific simulators, limited in environment variety (Arena 3.0 generated only three randomized environment types) and often built on outdated ROS1, which widens the sim2real gap.
motivation: Human-centric robot navigation needs reproducible, varied and realistic benchmarks with easy transfer to real robots. Prior surveys and guidelines (Francis et al., Singamaneni et al., Mirsky et al.) found comprehensive simulation platforms lacking. Generative models can produce diverse, controllable environments and scenarios on demand.
key_idea: Arena 4.0 is a fully ROS2-based, simulator-abstracted social navigation platform that generates human-centric 3D worlds from text prompts via an LLM, a GNN and a semantic 3D model database, with HuNavSim-based pedestrian scenarios.
insight: Splitting generation into an LLM stage (text to a 3D scene graph), a GNN stage (graph to floor plan and asset regions) and a semi-classical population stage lets the generative model's expressiveness be used while keeping placement modular. The generated-world statistics over 5000 worlds show that asset, doorway and room counts grow roughly linearly with the LLM-specified difficulty, so complexity scales without saturating up to about 25 rooms. The user study (20 participants) credits the simplified installer and world generation, but users found the web-based evaluation and plotting pipeline counterintuitive.
method: Arena-gen (Generation stage): an LLM converts a natural-language prompt into a machine-readable 3D scene graph (3DSG); a spatial GNN turns it into an annotated floor plan image and asset regions inside rooms.

3D Scene Graph and dataset: a 2-level hierarchical 3DSG (room-room connectivity plus room-asset relations with natural-language descriptions) is extracted from about 5000 CubiCasa5K floor plans, giving (3DSG, floor plan) pairs to train the GNN.

Population stage / Arena-Models: a prompt-queryable semantic vector database of models (over 100 obstacles, over 15 humans, over 30 color-material combinations) is queried by an Asset Placer, and a Fitter arranges the assets into zones. Output is Unity prefabs or COLLADA files, with a GUI explorer for annotation.

ROS2 migration: complete move to ROS2 Humble, Ubuntu 22, Nav2 (replacing move_base_flex) and Gazebo Garden, with a ROS2 dynamic map generator and a universal metrics recorder/evaluator; it supports ROS2-only robots such as Unitree Go2.

Scenario and human behavior generation: HuNavSim is integrated and extended with human-human and human-object interactions and semantic zones for sampling pedestrian behavior; Task Generator and Simulation-Setup use scene graphs and room segmentation.

Usability and benchmarking tooling: a monolithic installer, GUIs (Arena Architect, database explorer), full Docker image, and APIs for integrating planners; it was selected as the host platform of the SocialNav2025 competition.

setting.backbone: LLM (unspecified) for prompt to 3D scene graph + spatial GNN for floor plan/asset regions; Nav2 planners for navigation
setting.training_data: GNN trained on (3DSG, floor plan) pairs derived from CubiCasa5K (about 5000 real floor plans); LLM used as is
setting.observation: not applicable (simulation platform; robot sensors in Gazebo/Unity, ROS2 laser/maps)
setting.action_space: Nav2 velocity commands / planners (platform-level, not a fixed action space)

numbers_note: No navigation benchmark results. Evaluation is a 20-person user study (qualitative) plus generated-world statistics and generation latency reported only in figures.
results: World generation produces environments whose room, doorway and asset counts scale roughly linearly with input difficulty up to about 25-room worlds, with high graph connectivity and low diameter. The user study (20 participants) was mostly positive on installation and world generation. No navigation-performance comparison against baselines is reported.
limitations: No quantitative navigation benchmarking of planners on generated worlds; evaluation is a small user study and figure-based generated-world statistics.
Currently limited to Gazebo and Unity; Isaac Gym/Habitat support and real-robot deployment pipelines are left to future work.
The evaluation/plotting web interface was found counterintuitive by users, and the LLM-estimated difficulty is a latent, unvalidated measure.
